arabic text:
Bhayaa tumhe ghar jaake kahaa paayegi zainab
Pardes hai ghurbat hai, kahaa jayegi zainab
Tum saaniye Zahra ki, gharibi ko samajna
Ghazi ki qasam hai tumhe, bhaayi na tarap na
Be parda teri laash pe, jab ayegi zainab
english translation text:
Brother, where will Zainab find you when she returns home?
This is exile and utter loneliness—where will Zainab go?
Understand the helplessness of the second Zahra.
By Ghazi’s oath, brother, do not be distressed
when Zainab comes unveiled to your body.

arabic text: Kis tarha guzarungi, qayamat ka woh lamha\nJab shame gharibaan mein, mera saamna hoga\nBaba se nigahe na, mila payegi zainab
english translation text: How will I survive that moment of Judgement,\nwhen Shaam-e-Ghareeban confronts me?\nZainab will not be able to meet her father’s gaze.

arabic text: Insaaf karo kaise, behen dil ko sambhale\nIs tanz ka ehsaas, mujhe maar na dale,\nBaaghi ki bahen sham me, kehlaegi zainab
english translation text: Tell me fairly—how can a sister steady her heart?\nMay the sting of this taunt not kill me:\n“In Shaam, Zainab will be called the rebel’s sister.”

arabic text: Tum meri tarha gham ye, akele hi sahoge\nWaada karo ye baat na baano se kahoge\nZindaa me sakina jo dafnaegi zainab
english translation text: You too will bear this grief alone, as I do.\nPromise you will not tell Bano\nthat Zainab buried Sakina in the prison.

arabic text: Deti rahi jayengi wo maayus nigahe\nSughra jo use deti, hai jine ki duaaen\nAkber ke bina jab bhi, watan jaayegi zainab
english translation text: Those hopeless eyes will remain before me—\nSughra, who keeps praying for him to live—\nwhenever Zainab returns home without Akbar.

arabic text: Kyaa kya huwa bazaar mein, batlaaungi kaise\nAbdula e jafar ko, mein samjaaungi kaise\nJab neel e rasan ke unhe, dikhlaaegi zainab
english translation text: How will I describe all that happened in the marketplace?\nHow will I explain it to Abdullah ibn Jafar\nwhen Zainab shows him the bruises left by the rope?

arabic text: Bhaayi pe nazar karke, takalum wo pukari\nBhaya me samaj ti hoo tabiyat ko tumhari\nAchaa ye sada lab pe, nahi laayegi zainab
english translation text: Looking upon her brother, Takallum says she cried:\n“Brother, I understand the condition of your heart.\nVery well—Zainab will not utter that cry again.”
